subject: AIC arbitrarily penalizes higher numbers of surveys instead of actual parameters after building unmarkedMultFrame models

messages.author: 3f2b03987aa45f49
messages.subject: AIC arbitrarily penalizes higher numbers of surveys instead of actual parameters after building unmarkedMultFrame models
parts:
Hi everyone,

I'm having some issues when constructing an AIC table from unmarkedMultFrame models, and am concerned that I am parameterizing my models incorrectly. The dimensions of my data as a follows: 37 primary periods, 3 secondary periods within primary periods (so 111 total sampling events), and 7 study sites. I have several observational covariates, and am trying to see if models using any of these covariates explain my occupancy data better than a dot model. For each covariate, I have a data frame with 7 rows and 111 columns - so data from each site on each survey. These covariates collectively comprise the object "ObsCovs". I am able to create an unmarked framework just fine using these data, and even build different models using my covariates in an unmarked framework. The trouble arises when I go to compare my models using an AIC table. R tells me that my dot model has 4 parameters, while any models that use a single covariate to explain the data have a whopping 115 parameters. Clearly each of my columns is being counted as an additional parameter (4+111=115). This doesn't make any sense to me, because it seems like non-dot models are being arbitrarily penalized not because of the number of parameters, but because of the large number of sampling events. In other words, if I had say 70 columns (=70 surveys), my AIC table would say that a model using a single observational covariate to explain detection would have 74 parameters (4+70). The number of "parameters" R is calculating is mostly being influenced not by the number of covariates in my models, but by the number of columns in the matrix for each covariate used. How can I tell R to consider each covariate matrix as a single parameter instead of considering each column in each matrix its own parameter. Surely more sampling is better than less, so it doesn't make sense to me why my non-dot models would be penalized just because I did a lot of surveys.

Here is my code:

observation<-as.matrix(read.csv("Detection_Round2.csv", header=T))
weather<-as.matrix(read.csv("Weather_Round2.csv", header=T))
shannon<-as.matrix(read.csv("Diversity_Round2.csv", header=T))

###Create Unmarked data frame
y<-as.matrix(observation[,c(1:111)])
MinTemp<-as.matrix(weather[,c(1:111)])
MaxTemp<-as.matrix(weather[,c(112:222)])
MeanTemp<-as.matrix(weather[,c(223:333)])
Div<-as.matrix(shannon)
ObsCovs<-list(MinTemp=MinTemp, MaxTemp=MaxTemp, MeanTemp=MeanTemp, Div=Div)
umf<-unmarkedMultFrame(y=y,siteCovs=NULL, obsCovs=ObsCovs, numPrimary=37)

###Fit a few initial models
fm1<-colext(~1,~1,~1,~1, data=umf)
fm2<-colext(~ObsCovs$Div,~1,~1,~1, data=umf)
fm3<-colext(~ObsCovs$MeanTemp,~1,~1,~1, data=umf)

AICtable <- modSel(fitList(fm1, fm2, fm3))
AICtable

#################

Here is what my resulting AIC table looks like:

      nPars     AIC        delta      AICwt   cumltvWt
fm1     4      754.07    0.00     1.0e+00     1.00
fm2   115    969.00   214.93  2.1e-47      1.00
fm3   115    976.84   222.77  4.2e-49      1.00

Any help would be greatly appreciated!!

messages.author: d3fd439c2e48caf1
messages.subject: Re: AIC arbitrarily penalizes higher numbers of surveys instead of actual parameters after building unmarkedMultFrame models
parts:
Sky, I think you are unintentionally confusing colext with the use of ~ObsCovs$Div or ~ObsCovs$MeanTemp in your model formula. There isn't a reason I can see why you'd be calling a table from outside you unmarkedMultFrame. Your code looks good otherwise (assuming you don't get an error when you make your unmarkedMultFrame [umf<-unmarkedMultFrame( ...], so just use ~Div or ~MeanTemp in your model formula and (barring the unlikely possibility that Div or MeanTemp are in fact factors with 111 levels) you should be good to go.

Giancarlo

where umf is the unmarked data frame.

 

Thanks and best regards  - Marc

parts:
Dear Sky,

OK, so these observational covariates are indeed treated as continuous covariates, as they should. The way you wrote your model, they should count as one additional parameter each EXCEPT for one think, which I don't understand. Here is how you wrote your models:

###Fit a few initial models

fm1<-colext(~1,~1,~1,~1, data=umf)

fm2<-colext(~ObsCovs$Div,~1,~1,~1, data=umf)

fm3<-colext(~ObsCovs$MeanTemp,~1,~1,~1, data=umf)

According to the colext help page, the function usage is this:

colext(psiformula= ~1, gammaformula = ~ 1, epsilonformula = ~ 1, 
    pformula = ~ 1, data, starts, method="BFGS", se=TRUE, ...)

So, you seem to be fitting models that have these covariates in the (sub)model for initial detection, which of course does not make sense and which should throw an error
 (you can only have site-covariates for initial occupancy, that is, vectors of length 7). Can you try specifying the model in the correct way, e.g. like this ?

fm3<-colext(1,1,1, ~ObsCovs$MeanTemp,data=umf)

What does this yield ?

Regards  ---- Marc

On Tuesday, April 18, 2017 at 4:34:16 PM UTC-6, Sky Button wrote:

Hi everyone,

 

I'm having some issues when constructing an AIC table from unmarkedMultFrame models, and am concerned that I am parameterizing my models incorrectly. The dimensions of my data as a follows: 37 primary periods, 3 secondary periods within primary periods (so 111 total sampling events), and 7 study sites. I have several observational covariates, and am trying to see if models using any of these covariates explain my occupancy data better than a dot model. For each covariate, I have a data frame with 7 rows and 111 columns - so data from each site on each survey. These covariates collectively comprise the object "ObsCovs". I am able to create an unmarked framework just fine using these data, and even build different models using my covariates in an unmarked framework. The trouble arises when I go to compare my models using an AIC table. R tells me that my dot model has 4 parameters, while any models that use a single covariate to explain the data have a whopping 115 parameters. Clearly each of my columns is being counted as an additional parameter (4+111=115). This doesn't make any sense to me, because it seems like non-dot models are being arbitrarily penalized not because of the number of parameters, but because of the large number of sampling events. In other words, if I had say 70 columns (=70 surveys), my AIC table would say that a model using a single observational covariate to explain detection would have 74 parameters (4+70). The number of "parameters" R is calculating is mostly being influenced not by the number of covariates in my models, but by the number of columns in the matrix for each covariate used. How can I tell R to consider each covariate matrix as a single parameter instead of considering each column in each matrix its own parameter. Surely more sampling is better than less, so it doesn't make sense to me why my non-dot models would be penalized just because I did a lot of surveys.

 

Here is my code:

 

observation<-as.matrix(read.csv("Detection_Round2.csv", header=T))

weather<-as.matrix(read.csv("Weather_Round2.csv", header=T))

shannon<-as.matrix(read.csv("Diversity_Round2.csv", header=T))

 

###Create Unmarked data frame

y<-as.matrix(observation[,c(1:111)])

MinTemp<-as.matrix(weather[,c(1:111)])

MaxTemp<-as.matrix(weather[,c(112:222)])

MeanTemp<-as.matrix(weather[,c(223:333)])

Div<-as.matrix(shannon)

ObsCovs<-list(MinTemp=MinTemp, MaxTemp=MaxTemp, MeanTemp=MeanTemp, Div=Div)

umf<-unmarkedMultFrame(y=y,siteCovs=NULL, obsCovs=ObsCovs, numPrimary=37)

 

###Fit a few initial models

fm1<-colext(~1,~1,~1,~1, data=umf)

fm2<-colext(~ObsCovs$Div,~1,~1,~1, data=umf)

fm3<-colext(~ObsCovs$MeanTemp,~1,~1,~1, data=umf)

 

AICtable <- modSel(fitList(fm1, fm2, fm3))

AICtable

 

#################

 

Here is what my resulting AIC table looks like:

 

      nPars     AIC        delta      AICwt   cumltvWt

fm1     4      754.07    0.00     1.0e+00     1.00

fm2   115    969.00   214.93  2.1e-47      1.00

fm3   115    976.84   222.77  4.2e-49      1.00

 

Any help would be greatly appreciated!!

Dear Sky,

I am somewhat relieved that unmarked seems to be doing what it should. I think that it is an error that colext fitted any model in the way you specified it: it ought to be impossible to fit the effect of an observational covariate on initial occupancy. This seems to point to a bug.

As to your many questions: to be honest, you should read a couple of standard intro occupancy papers or a book chapter or two. I bet the answer to all of them will be immediately apparent upon doing some homework. The list is not the place to ask such basic things.

Best regards  ---- Marc

On Wednesday, April 19, 2017 at 10:00:03 AM UTC-5, Kery Marc wrote:
Dear Sky,

OK, so these observational covariates are indeed treated as continuous covariates, as they should. The way you wrote your model, they should count as one additional parameter each EXCEPT for one think, which I don't understand. Here is how you wrote your models:

###Fit a few initial models

fm1<-colext(~1,~1,~1,~1, data=umf)

fm2<-colext(~ObsCovs$Div,~1,~1,~1, data=umf)

fm3<-colext(~ObsCovs$MeanTemp,~1,~1,~1, data=umf)

 

According to the colext help page, the function usage is this:

colext(psiformula= ~1, gammaformula = ~ 1, epsilonformula = ~ 1, 
    pformula = ~ 1, data, starts, method="BFGS", se=TRUE, ...)

So, you seem to be fitting models that have these covariates in the (sub)model for initial detection, which of course does not make sense and which should throw an error
 (you can only have site-covariates for initial occupancy, that is, vectors of length 7). Can you try specifying the model in the correct way, e.g. like this ?

fm3<-colext(1,1,1, ~ObsCovs$MeanTemp,data=umf)

What does this yield ?

Regards  ---- Marc

On Tuesday, April 18, 2017 at 4:34:16 PM UTC-6, Sky Button wrote:

Hi everyone,

 

I'm having some issues when constructing an AIC table from unmarkedMultFrame models, and am concerned that I am parameterizing my models incorrectly. The dimensions of my data as a follows: 37 primary periods, 3 secondary periods within primary periods (so 111 total sampling events), and 7 study sites. I have several observational covariates, and am trying to see if models using any of these covariates explain my occupancy data better than a dot model. For each covariate, I have a data frame with 7 rows and 111 columns - so data from each site on each survey. These covariates collectively comprise the object "ObsCovs". I am able to create an unmarked framework just fine using these data, and even build different models using my covariates in an unmarked framework. The trouble arises when I go to compare my models using an AIC table. R tells me that my dot model has 4 parameters, while any models that use a single covariate to explain the data have a whopping 115 parameters. Clearly each of my columns is being counted as an additional parameter (4+111=115). This doesn't make any sense to me, because it seems like non-dot models are being arbitrarily penalized not because of the number of parameters, but because of the large number of sampling events. In other words, if I had say 70 columns (=70 surveys), my AIC table would say that a model using a single observational covariate to explain detection would have 74 parameters (4+70). The number of "parameters" R is calculating is mostly being influenced not by the number of covariates in my models, but by the number of columns in the matrix for each covariate used. How can I tell R to consider each covariate matrix as a single parameter instead of considering each column in each matrix its own parameter. Surely more sampling is better than less, so it doesn't make sense to me why my non-dot models would be penalized just because I did a lot of surveys.

 

Here is my code:

 

observation<-as.matrix(read.csv("Detection_Round2.csv", header=T))

weather<-as.matrix(read.csv("Weather_Round2.csv", header=T))

shannon<-as.matrix(read.csv("Diversity_Round2.csv", header=T))

 

###Create Unmarked data frame

y<-as.matrix(observation[,c(1:111)])

MinTemp<-as.matrix(weather[,c(1:111)])

MaxTemp<-as.matrix(weather[,c(112:222)])

MeanTemp<-as.matrix(weather[,c(223:333)])

Div<-as.matrix(shannon)

ObsCovs<-list(MinTemp=MinTemp, MaxTemp=MaxTemp, MeanTemp=MeanTemp, Div=Div)

umf<-unmarkedMultFrame(y=y,siteCovs=NULL, obsCovs=ObsCovs, numPrimary=37)

 

###Fit a few initial models

fm1<-colext(~1,~1,~1,~1, data=umf)

fm2<-colext(~ObsCovs$Div,~1,~1,~1, data=umf)

fm3<-colext(~ObsCovs$MeanTemp,~1,~1,~1, data=umf)

 

AICtable <- modSel(fitList(fm1, fm2, fm3))

AICtable

 

#################

 

Here is what my resulting AIC table looks like:
